facts.statement: The premaxillae of Mymoorapelta probably formed a narrow, toothed, and trapezoidal muzzle similar to Gargoyleosaurus.

facts.statement: Nodosaurid teeth, including those of Mymoorapelta, were blade-like, larger, and more complex than ankylosaurid teeth, featuring rough enamel and a crenelated cingulum.
facts.quote: Nodosaurid teeth are blade-like, larger, and usually more complex than the basic cusps of ankylosaurids, having a larger crown, a rough enamel surface, confluent fluting with grooves of the marginal cusps, and a crenelated cingulum (shelf-like bulge surrounding the base of a tooth crown)

facts.statement: It is debated whether an osteoderm from New Mexico belongs to Mymoorapelta, as it is morphologically similar but stratigraphically closer to Gargoyleosaurus.
facts.quote: The osteoderm is morphologically (based on external anatomy) similar to Mymoorapelta, however it is stratigraphically (based on rock layers) closer to Gargoyleosaurus

facts.statement: A large portion of the postcranial skeleton of Mymoorapelta has been discovered.
facts.quote: A large part of the postcranial (behind the skull) skeleton of Mymoorapelta is known.

facts.statement: The neck vertebrae of Mymoorapelta have centra that are wider than tall with a heart-shaped morphology.
facts.quote: In the cervicals, the faces (ends) of the centra are wider than they are tall and display a heart-shaped morphology.

facts.statement: Mymoorapelta possesses 13 ribs with triangular cross-sections and a weak T-shape, differing from other ankylosaurs.
facts.quote: Mymoorapelta has 13 ribs, all of which have triangular cross-sections and a weak T-shape, in contrast to other ankylosaurs.

facts.statement: Mymoorapelta is one of the few ankylosaurs known to have four sacral ribs.
facts.quote: Mymoorapelta is also one of the few ankylosaurs with 4 sacral ribs, a trait it shares with only 3 other taxa.

facts.statement: The vertebral centra and neural spines of Mymoorapelta are significantly shorter than those of Gargoyleosaurus.
facts.quote: The vertebral centra and neural spines are much shorter when compared to Gargoyleosaurus.

facts.statement: A preserved chevron in Mymoorapelta measures 9.1 cm in length and curves strongly backward.
facts.quote: One of the preserved chevrons measures 9.1 cm and is strongly recurved posteriorly.

facts.statement: The ulna in Mymoorapelta features a broad, massive olecranon process with preserved surface roughness.
facts.quote: In the forelimbs, the ulna has a broad, massive olecranon process that preserves rugosities.

facts.statement: Mymoorapelta has short, wide foot bones with long, triangular, and pointed toe bones, unlike other nodosaurids such as Edmontonia.
facts.quote: In the pes (foot), the genus preserves short, wide metapodials with long phalanges, with the distal phalanges looking triangular and pointed in side view, contrary to other nodosaurids like Edmontonia.

facts.statement: Mymoorapelta was characterized by large spiked osteoderms protruding from the sides and back of its body.
facts.quote: A prominent feature of Mymoorapelta was its armor, which mostly consisted of large spiked osteoderms (bony armor) protruding from the lateral and dorsal sides of the body.

facts.statement: Five distinct types of armor have been preserved in Mymoorapelta, including spines, plates, bladelike spines, flat scutes, and fused plates.
facts.quote: In Mymoorapelta, there are five different preserved armor types: elongated spines with a large, hollow base; thin triangular plates with a narrow, asymmetrical base; small bladelike spines with a rounded, solid base; isolated, flat, keeled scutes; and scutes fused into a single plate of armor.

facts.statement: A preserved triangular armor plate from Mymoorapelta measures 11 cm in length.
facts.quote: A specimen of Mymoorapelta preserves one of these at 11 cm in length.

facts.statement: Twelve keeled, flat scutes recovered from Mymoorapelta in 1994 show an oval shape with weak pitting but lack neurovascular grooves and foramina.
facts.quote: Twelve of the previously mentioned keeled, flat scutes were recovered from a specimen of Mymoorapelta in 1994, they preserve a keeled oval shape and an external surface that bears uniform, weak pitting, and a privation of neurovascular grooves (the system that controls blood flow and homeostasis) and foramina (small openings within bones).

facts.statement: The sacral shield of Mymoorapelta contains two middle rows of larger scutes, with seven scutes in each row.
facts.quote: The sacral shield also preserves two middle rows of larger scutes, with each row preserving seven.

facts.statement: Estimates based on a Cactus Park specimen suggest the complete sacral shield of Mymoorapelta was 70 cm wide for a 50 cm wide pelvis.
facts.quote: A more complete sacral shield was preserved in the Cactus Park specimen, with estimates placing the complete sacral shield at 70 cm in width for a pelvis that is 50 cm wide.

facts.statement: Mymoorapelta possesses a category 2 sacral shield characterized by bosses bordering tubercles and rosettes of fused osteoderms.
facts.quote: Mymoorapelta preserves a category 2 sacral shield, which is characterized by bosses (keeled osteoderms) that border tubercles (elevated knobs) as well as rosettes of co-ossified osteoderms.

facts.statement: Mymoorapelta had solid conical armor, whereas Gargoyleosaurus had thin-walled armor.
facts.quote: The armor of Mymoorapelta differs from that of Gargoyleosaurus in that the former has solid conical armor compared to the thin-walled armor of the latter.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that category 1 sacral shields might represent a growth stage of category 2 shields, similar to traits seen in modern armadillos and alligators.
facts.quote: Victoria Arbour et al. (2011) suggested that category 1 shields could simply be an ontogenetic (growth) stage of category 2, as they have very similar morphology but are not co-ossified, which is an ontogenetic trait present in extant armored animals like armadillos and alligators.

facts.statement: Mymoorapelta was a low-browsing herbivore that likely fed on ferns, cycads, and conifers.
facts.quote: Mymoorapelta was a low-browsing herbivore like its relatives, likely feeding on the ferns, cycads, and conifers that dominated the flora of its time due to the lack of complex grasses in the Jurassic.

facts.statement: Mymoorapelta had a narrow snout, an adaptation for selective browsing rather than grazing.
facts.quote: Nodosaurids like Mymoorapelta had narrow snouts, an adaptation seen today in animals that are selective browsers as opposed to the wide muzzles of grazers.

facts.statement: Evidence from related ankylosaurs suggests Mymoorapelta had fleshy, muscular tongues that could assist in feeding on low-growing plants.
facts.quote: The preservation of complete a hyoid in taxa like the ankylosaurid Pinacosaurus and the nodosaurid Edmontonia demonstrate that ankylosaurs had fleshy, muscular tongues that could have assisted with feeding on plants that grew low to the ground.

facts.statement: Related nodosaurids had fleshy cheeks and cheek plates that covered tooth rows for defense and to prevent food loss while eating.
facts.quote: The preservation of cheek plates in Edmontonia and Panoplosaurus provide evidence for fleshy cheeks and chewing, with the cheek covering the tooth rows both for defense and to prevent food loss when eating.

facts.statement: Direct evidence of tooth occlusion has not been preserved in Mymoorapelta.
facts.quote: Tooth occlusion is not directly preserved in Mymoorapelta or its close relative Gargoyleosaurus, but it has been found in other nodosaurids from the Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Mymoorapelta may have had a varied diet including tough leaves and pulpy fruits, despite not feeding on fibrous and woody plants.
facts.quote: Even though ankylosaurs may not have fed on fibrous and woody plants, they may have had a varied diet which included tough leaves and pulpy fruits.

facts.statement: Mymoorapelta appears adapted for open environments due to competition with diplodocid sauropods.
facts.quote: Due to competition with diplodocid sauropods, Mymoorapelta seems more adapted for open environments.

facts.statement: Mymoorapelta has a limited known distribution found at two sites in Western Colorado, plus the Hanksville-Burpee and potential Albuquerque specimens.
facts.quote: Mymoorapelta has a very limited known distribution, having only been found at two sites in Western Colorado, in addition to the Hanksville-Burpee and potential Albuquerque specimens.

facts.statement: Taphonomy of the Hanksville-Burpee specimen suggests Mymoorapelta died inland, contrary to previous inferences of a coastal distribution for nodosaurids.
facts.quote: The Hanksville-Burpee specimen's taphonomy (how and where it decomposed to end up as a fossil) suggests that the individual had died inland, contrary to the coastal distribution previously inferred for nodosaurids.

facts.statement: Reconstructions by Coombs in 1978 suggest Mymoorapelta's forelimbs bore most of its weight and were adapted for high force delivery, possibly for food gathering.
facts.quote: Reconstructions of ankylosaur forelimb musculature made by Coombs in 1978 suggest that the forelimbs bore the majority of the animal's weight and that they were adapted for high force delivery on the front feet, possibly for food gathering.

facts.statement: Coombs suggested ankylosaurs may have been capable diggers, though their hoof-like manus would have limited fossorial capabilities.
facts.quote: Coombs suggested that ankylosaurs may have been capable diggers, though the hoof-like structure of the manus would have limited fossorial capabilities.

facts.statement: While the tail was thought to be used for defense against predators, recent findings suggest it might have been used for intraspecific combat, a possibility that might apply to basal taxa like Mymoorapelta.
facts.quote: It is thought that the tail could also have been used in defense against predators, though more recent findings by Arbour et al. in 2022 also consider the possibility that the tails of ankylosaurids were used for intraspecific combat and might have primarily evolved to fill a function here, which might indicate a similar use in more basal taxa like Mymoorapelta and Gargoyleosaurus.

facts.statement: The clade Nodosauridae was named in 1890 by Othniel Charles Marsh, who designated Nodosaurus as the type genus.
facts.quote: The clade was named in 1890 by Othniel Charles Marsh, who designated the Cretaceous genus Nodosaurus as the type genus based on the heavy dermal armor, solid bones, large forelimbs, and ungulate feet it preserves.

facts.statement: Nodosaurids first evolved in the Late Jurassic (ca. 155 mya), with Mymoorapelta being an early member of this evolutionary radiation.
facts.quote: Nodosaurids first evolved in the Late Jurassic (ca. 155 mya), with Mymoorapelta and the similarly sized Gargoyleosaurus being early members of the evolutionary radiation which would continue into the Cretaceous in accordance with Cope's Rule.

facts.statement: Nodosaurids differ from ankylosaurids by having osteoderm-lined, flexible tails and sacral shields, whereas ankylosaurids evolved more recently and lack mace-like tail clubs.
facts.quote: Nodosaurids differ from ankylosaurids in the fact that ankylosaurids evolved more recently, during the Early Cretaceous, and in several distinct anatomical characteristics; most notably the lack of mace-like tail clubs, with nodosaurs having osteoderm-lined, flexible tails instead, and the possession of sacral shields.

facts.statement: The proposed family Polacanthidae has seen little support from recent phylogenetic analyses and is in a state of flux.
facts.quote: However, it has seen little support from phylogenetic analyses in recent years and is in a state of flux.

facts.statement: A 2010 phylogenetic analysis placed Mymoorapelta as the sister taxon to Gargoyleosaurus in a group outside of Polacanthidae, Nodosauridae, and Ankylosauridae.
facts.quote: A 2010 phylogenetic analysis utilizing undescribed material resulted with Mymoorapelta as the sister taxon to Gargoyleosaurus in their own group outside of Polacanthidae, Nodosauridae, and Ankylosauridae.

facts.statement: A 2018 analysis by Rivera-Sylva and colleagues recovered Mymoorapelta as a basal nodosaurid in a clade with Sauroplites and Dongyangopelta, representing the most basal group within Nodosauridae.
facts.quote: In a 2018 phylogenetic analysis by Rivera-Sylva and colleagues which has been reproduced below, Mymoorapelta is recovered as a basal nodosaurid in a clade with Sauroplites and Dongyangopelta that represents the most basal group within Nodosauridae, while Gargoyleosaurus is recovered as more derived, further proving their distinction.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Mymoorapelta may be an ankylosaur outside both Nodosauridae and Ankylosauridae.
facts.quote: Alternatively, Mymoorapelta may also be an ankylosaur outside both Nodosauridae and Ankylosauridae.
